items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: the man we had to place, Bush Hall, was a fellow by the name of Albert Dominick, known as Don Alick.

ctx.x: Yeah. Did his father have a nickname?

Yeah, that's what I'm trying to think now. His father's nickname used to call him, I can't think of a president name. But anyhow, he was, I was financial secretary of the local. And then we kept that organization until Bush died. Then Dwight Newman, the piano player, he took the band over. And then we first, the man we had to place, Bush Hall, was a fellow by the name of Albert Dominick, known as Don Alick. Oh, yeah. Don Albert, yeah. I think he's now living in El Paso, Texas. In later years he formed a big large…
We must try to remember to talk to his father is still living here. He's still living here.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: That's right, Lloyd Contrell, and a fella by the name of Don Albert.

ctx.x: And then we made it, uh, our band, eight-piece band, and we put Lloyd Contrell. And the president of the local, he was, he was the first band he ever played with.
